items.title: Standard Working Hours
items.text: The statutory work week in Togo is 40 hours. Overtime is capped and requires premium pay (+20% for first 8 hours).

items.title: Termination and Notice
items.text: Notice periods vary by seniority: 8 days for laborers, up to 3 months for executives. Improper dismissal leads to high court damages.

items.title: Annual Leave Entitlement
items.text: Employees earn 1.5 days of paid leave per month (18 days/year), increasing with tenure (extra 2 days after 15 years).

items.title: Probation Rules
items.text: Probation is limited to 6 months for managers and 1-3 months for others, renewable once in writing.

items.title: Severance Pay
items.text: Severance is due after 1 year of service for CDI contracts, based on a percentage of monthly salary per year served.

items.title: Maternity Leave
items.description: 14 weeks of partially paid leave (8 weeks post-natal), often supplemented by CNSS payments.

items.title: Sick Leave
items.description: Payment for the first few days of certified illness, transitioning to social security coverage.

items.title: 13th Month Bonus
items.description: Customary in Togo, typically paid in December to coincide with festivities.

items.title: Transport Allowance
items.description: Statutory requirement to contribute towards commuting costs, often partially tax-exempt.

items.title: Medical Insurance
items.description: While AMU is mandatory, many international firms provide private supplemental top-up plans.

faqs.question: Can I pay in USD?
faqs.answer: The contract can be pegged to USD, but actual disbursement must be in XOF to ensure compliant social filings.

faqs.question: How long is the onboarding?
faqs.answer: Typically 5-10 business days once all documents are received.

faqs.question: Are background checks allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, criminal record checks (Casier Judiciaire) are standard for sensitive roles.

faqs.question: What is the SMIG?
faqs.answer: The minimum wage (Salaire Minimum Interprofessionnel Garanti) is currently XOF 52,500 per month.

faqs.question: Can EOR hire expats?
faqs.answer: Yes, but requires a work permit and proof that the skills aren't locally available.

steps.title: Data Gathering

steps.title: Tax Calculation
steps.description: Applying IRPP progressive rates and calculating social security subtractions.

steps.title: Payslip Generation
steps.description: Issuing the 'Bulletin de Paie' in French with required tax IDs (NIF).

steps.title: Funding & Payouts
steps.description: Transferring XAF to local employee bank accounts (Ecobank, UTB) by month-end.

steps.title: Statutory Filings
steps.description: Submitting the DISI (Social) and IRPP (Tax) to OTR by the 15th of next month.

items.title: Late Filing Penalties
items.text: Failing to pay OTR/CNSS by the 15th results in 5% instant surcharge plus 1% monthly interest.

items.title: Tax Free Allowances
items.text: Transport and housing allowances have specific non-taxable thresholds defined by the General Tax Code.

items.title: Electronic Portals
items.text: The OTR requires digital filing for most enterprises via 'SYDONIA' or equivalent platforms.

items.title: Record Keeping
items.text: Payroll records must be archived for at least 10 years for potential audit purposes.

items.title: CNSS Caps
items.text: The CNSS contribution is capped at a monthly ceiling (currently XOF 400,000 for some components).

faqs.question: How often is payroll?
faqs.answer: Monthly, usually arriving in accounts between the 25th and 30th.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, performance and year-end bonuses are taxed as standard income.

faqs.question: Can we use overseas banks?
faqs.answer: While funding can come from abroad, payments must arrive in local currency (XOF) to employee accounts.

faqs.question: Is payslip digital authorized?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided it is signed/stamped if requested by local authorities.

faqs.question: Work permit cost?
faqs.answer: Varies by nationality; ECOWAS nationals have easier processing.

steps.title: Define Gross Base
steps.description: Starting with the negotiated monthly salary in XAF.

steps.title: Add Allowances
steps.description: Including taxable housing or utility benefits.

steps.title: Subtract Social (9%)
steps.description: Deducting employee share for CNSS and AMU.

steps.title: Apply IRPP Brackets
steps.description: Calculating income tax on the remaining balance.

steps.title: Apply CAC Surcharge
steps.description: Adding the 7% local municipal tax on the calculated IRPP.

steps.title: Final Net Disbursement
steps.description: The amount transferred to the local bank account.

items.title: SMIG Guardrail
items.text: Gross < 52,500 XAF is non-compliant in Togo.

items.title: Family Deductions
items.text: IRPP decreases based on number of children (Charge de Famille).

items.title: Transport Exemptions
items.text: First 30,000 XAF of transport allowance is subtracted from the taxable base.

items.title: Overtime Premiums
items.text: Overtime pay is added to gross and taxed normally.

items.title: Professional Expenses
items.text: A standard 20% flat abatement applies to some salary components for professional costs.

faqs.answer: High-confidence estimate; final payslips may vary slightly by rounding.

faqs.question: Does it include 13th month?
faqs.answer: You must input it as a specific bonus month.

faqs.question: What about day rates?
faqs.answer: Optimized for monthly; divide by 26 for daily estimate.

faqs.question: Are HQ benefits included?
faqs.answer: Only if they are deemed taxable in-kind benefits in Togo.

faqs.question: Frequency?
faqs.answer: Monthly calculations as per Togo labor law.

items.text: Most common; requires 1+ shareholders. Management is flexible under the OHADA framework.

items.title: SA (Public Ltd)
items.text: Higher capital (10M XOF). Mandatory for banking, insurance, and large industrial firms.

items.text: Valid for 2 years; must be converted to a local subsidiary or closed after the term expires.

items.title: Annual Tax License

items.title: Free Zone status

items.title: Board Members

faqs.question: What is OHADA?
faqs.answer: The regional business law that harmonizes legal systems across 17 African countries.

faqs.question: Need a local partner?
faqs.answer: No local partner requirement for SARL formation.
